Fact.Name: The numeric box 8 divisor is the same number the MeF String says
Fact.Description:
THE TIE. A second, numeric intake for a box the payer already reported as a String must not be able to disagree with it. The Match limit on form1099Rs:../writableOtherPercentage admits exactly four spellings of any one percentage - "50", "50.0", "50.00", "50.000" - so the test is an Any over those four. This is the box 8 twin of the shipping ../box9aDivisorTiesToMefString and is built to the same shape for the same reason.
THE TIE IS EXACT AND TWO-WAY. The divisor is rendered ONCE at scale 3 - exact, because ../box8PercentageAsRational is an integer number of thousandths over 1000 and has nothing to round - and each arm pads the String out to the same three decimal places before comparing. Only one arm can match a given String, since the four padded forms have four different lengths. Comparing the other way round, AsDecimalString at scales 0 through 3, would NOT be two-way: its setScale is HALF_UP, so a divisor of 50.4 renders "50" at scale 0 and would tie to a String that says something else.
A SPELLING THAT TIES FALSE ON PURPOSE: a leading zero. "05" is not one of the four renderings AsDecimalString produces for 5, so a String written "05" never matches any arm however correct the numeric divisor is, and the return REFUSES. That is the safe direction and it costs nothing: normalising the String is the application's job, not a place for the engine to guess that two spellings mean one number.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, on the ../box8FilesOnForm4972 pattern: both IsComplete legs come before any value read, so a return that has answered neither box resolves FALSE rather than Incomplete and the guard that reads it keeps its own completeness.

Fact.Name: This form's Form 4972 line 11 is grossed up by the box 8 percentage
Fact.Description:
THE POPULATION GATE for the box 8 half of Form 4972's multiple-recipient procedure, and the predicate /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage now counts the absence of. SEVEN conjuncts in SIX numbered groups - group (5) is two of them - in this order and for these reasons.
(1) IsComplete on form1099Rs:../writableBox8PercentageThousandths, first, so that a return that has not answered the numeric intake resolves FALSE here rather than dragging Incomplete into Form 4972 line 11. (2) form1099Rs:../causesRetirementBox8PercentageKO, which is TRUE exactly when the MeF String is answered and has a character outside "0." - a box 8 percentage of "0" or "0.000" is not a share and is not counted, which is also why nothing here can divide by zero through that door. (3) ../box8DivisorTiesToMefString, so a divisor that contradicts the transmitted String scales nothing. (4) a literal GreaterThan zero on the intake, which conjunct (2) already implies through the tie but which is stated anyway, because "no Divide in this module can see a zero divisor" should be readable at the division site. (5) THE BOX 8 AMOUNT ITSELF, complete and positive - two conjuncts, the IsComplete before the value read as everywhere else here: the payer enters the percentage "along with the current actuarial value" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16), so a percentage with no amount is a payer contradiction and stays refused rather than grossing up a zero.
(6) ../box9aMrdDivisionApplies, AND THIS IS THE CONJUNCT THAT MAKES THE NARROWING SAFE. Form 4972's Step 2 is ONE step with TWO divisions: box 2a by the box 9a percentage onto line 8, and box 8 by the box 8 percentage onto line 11. Line 12 adds line 10 (which carries line 8) to line 11. Grossing up line 11 while line 10 stayed at this recipient's share would build the same mixed-scale line 12 that ../box9aMrdBox8ContradictionRefusesThisReturn exists to refuse, arrived at from the other side. Requiring the box 9a procedure to be running means the two halves of Step 2 either both apply or neither does. A BOX 8 PERCENTAGE WITHOUT A BOX 9a PERCENTAGE THEREFORE STILL REFUSES, and that is deliberate: the printed procedure is entered only when "a percentage will be shown in Form 1099-R, boxes 8 and/or 9a" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 3) and it has no arm that divides line 11 without dividing line 8.
NOT A CONJUNCT, and named so silence is not read as coverage: the Part III election. Reading ../form4972PartIIITaxIsComputed here would be a CYCLE - it reads ../form4972InputsComplete, which reads IsComplete(../form4972Line11), which reads ../box8RoutesToForm4972Line11, which reads this fact. The Part-II-only or no-4972 return is NOT counted by this guard: with no election conjunct the gate is TRUE on that return, so the item is dropped from THIS guard's count and the return is caught one guard over instead, by /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Value through ../box8OtherAmountUseIsUndetermined. The cycle's real cost is UNDER-restriction (the gate cannot confine itself to Part III), not over-refusal; the refusal that covers the non-Part-III population lives on the VALUE guard, and that dependency is why the box8Value contract's cells (2)/(3) must not be retired while this gate reads no election. The LTC conjunct below is the same review's BLOCKER repair: a code-W form whose charge is applied routes AWAY from line 11, so without Not(../box8IsLongTermCareInvestmentReduction) a payer-contradictory form (an LTC charge carrying a multiple-recipient percentage) would slip BOTH this guard and the routing and file - the only return-level refusal of a non-zero box 8 percentage would go silent.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: both IsComplete legs come before every value read, and the three facts it reads are themselves complete-safe.
THIS FACT'S BODY IS UNCHANGED and the sentence opening this Description - "the predicate /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage now counts the absence of" - is the one line that is no longer literally true. That guard's Not() now reads ../box8PercentageEntryConsistent, a new wrapper placed immediately above this fact, whose second Any() arm IS this fact; so every item this fact frees the guard still frees, and the wrapper only adds the Part-II-only / no-Form-4972 escape that cannot be written here without the cycle named above. ../box8RoutesToForm4972Line11 and ../box8CurrentActuarialValueForForm4972 still read THIS fact directly and are unaffected - that is precisely why the escape sits one layer up rather than inside these seven conjuncts, which would have fed an Incomplete ../box8RecipientShareFraction into a live Divide.
CONJUNCT (6) IS LICENSED BY THE PRINTED SOURCES, NOT ONLY BY THE MIXED-SCALE ARGUMENT. THIS FACT'S BODY IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. The paragraph on conjunct (6) above ends "A BOX 8 PERCENTAGE WITHOUT A BOX 9a PERCENTAGE THEREFORE STILL REFUSES, and that is deliberate", and supports it with the mixed-scale harm plus the entry condition at f4972 lines 174-178. Residue (a) of the rebody contract at form1099Rs:/knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage treated that refusal as an OPEN cell, to be discharged either by a printed rule for the box-8-only share or by proving the combination cannot arise on a correctly prepared form. THE SECOND PROOF IS ON DISK IN ITS WEAKER AND SUFFICIENT FORM and is set out here, so the conjunct is no longer a design choice that a later unit might relax; it is what the instructions require.
THE STRONG CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD AND IS NOT MADE, corrected at the adversarial review before this append landed. A box 8 percentage beside a BLANK box 9a CAN appear on a correctly prepared form: box 9a is excused "for any IRA distributions or for a direct rollover" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16), the box 8 percentage instruction at lines 1097-1100 carries no matching carve-out, and a partly-direct-rolled distribution is reported on SEPARATE Forms 1099-R for each part (lines 1105-1107), so a code G form carrying an annuity contract out of a multiple-recipient lump sum is a correctly prepared box-8-only document. THE CLAIM ACTUALLY MADE IS NARROWER AND IS WHAT THIS CONJUNCT NEEDS: such a form is never in the population where Form 4972 line 11 is computed, and this conjunct is only reached there. Steps (1) through (4) below establish that; step (5) establishes that even inside the population no printed rule computes the combination.
(1) The box 8 percentage is entered ONLY when "an annuity contract is part of a multiple recipient lump-sum distribution" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16, RIGHT column). (2) That distribution is a lump-sum distribution, which Form 4972 defines as "the distribution or payment in 1 tax year of a plan participant's entire balance from all of an employer's qualified plans of one kind" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 2) - the same event box 2b calls a total distribution, "one or more distributions within 1 tax year in which the entire balance of the account is distributed" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 13). (3) Box 9a's entry condition is "If this is a total distribution and it is made to more than one person" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16); (1) supplies "more than one person" and (2) supplies "total distribution", so the box 9a condition is met wherever the box 8 condition is. THE ONE INFERENTIAL HINGE, named rather than hidden: box 9a's "this is a total distribution and it is made to more than one person" is read as the PLAN-LEVEL event split among recipients, which is the only reading under which a single recipient's Form 1099-R can be described as "made to more than one person" at all, and it is the reading the box 9a caption itself takes ("enter the percentage received by the person whose name appears on Form 1099-R"). (4) Box 9a's two carve-outs, "You need not complete this box for any IRA distributions or for a direct rollover" (i1099r lines 1117-1119), are both outside the Form 4972 population: "A distribution from an IRA" is an item of the "Distributions That Don't Qualify for the 20% Capital Gain Election or the 10-Year Tax Option" list (f4972 lines 150-158 heading, line 82 bullet), and a rollover fails that list from both sides - partially rolled over, "The part of a distribution not rolled over if the distribution is partially rolled over to another qualified plan or an IRA" is in the same list (f4972 lines 160-162); wholly directly rolled over, nothing remains of the "ordinary income part of the distribution" that the box 8 value is confined to figuring tax on (f4972 lines 74-78). (5) INDEPENDENTLY: the printed procedure contains no arm that grosses up line 11 without grossing up line 8. Step 2's box 8 bullet is its THIRD bullet, reached only past the two that divide box 2a by the box 9a percentage (f4972 lines 192-197 and 206-210); Step 3 pairs the same two divisions for the NUA election (lines 174-197 RIGHT column, the box 8 bullet at 206-209); Step 5 multiplies the tax back down by the box 9a percentage (lines 205-213 RIGHT column). So the combination has no printed computation even if it is transmitted.
WHAT FOLLOWS. The refusal conjunct (6) produces is permanent and correct, and it is TWO shapes rather than one: a PAYER CONTRADICTION (the mirror image of ../box9aMrdBox8ContradictionRefusesThisReturn, which was built for a box 9a percentage with a box 8 amount and no box 8 percentage on the identical i1099r sentence), OR a FILER ELECTING PART III on a distribution that does not qualify for the election - which is what the carve-out forms named above become the moment ../form4972TenYearElectionMade is true on them. Refusing is right in both shapes and for different reasons, and naming only the first is the overreach the review caught. No mirror FACT is minted here: that direction needed one because ../box9aEntryConsistent had to read it, whereas this direction is already refused by the absence of ../box8PercentageEntryConsistent, and a named boolean with no reader is documentation in fact form. This separates the contradiction from the box 9a data-completeness case that shares the conjunct: a return whose box 9a String is never answered is refused, and one whose box 9a String "50" is answered but form1099Rs:../writableBox9aPercentageThousandths is not is refused until it is answered; with it answered, the same return files.

Fact.Name: Box 8 percentage this return can carry without misstating a figure
Fact.Description:
THE GUARD-FACING GATE for the box 8 percentage, one layer above the mechanics gate. /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage counts the ABSENCE of this fact, where it used to count the absence of ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies directly. The layering mirrors ../box9aEntryConsistent, which sits outside ../box9aMrdDivisionApplies for the identical reason: an escape placed INSIDE the mechanics gate would feed an Incomplete ../box8RecipientShareFraction into the live Divide in ../box8CurrentActuarialValueForForm4972. ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies, ../box8RoutesToForm4972Line11 and ../box8CurrentActuarialValueForForm4972 are therefore untouched by this fact and keep reading each other exactly as before.
WHAT THE SECOND ARM IS. ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies unchanged: whenever the gross-up genuinely applies, the item was never counted and still is not.
WHAT THE FIRST ARM FREES, and why it is the narrow population and not the one the records prose describes. Form 4972 line 11 is a PART III line - lines 8 through 30 are the only lines that read it (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 1), and line 11's own text is "Current actuarial value of annuity from Form 1099-R, box 8. If none, enter -0-" (line 40). On a return that elects Part II only, or elects no Form 4972 treatment at all, line 11 is INERT: nothing divides the box 8 amount by the box 8 percentage because nothing reads the quotient. Requiring form1099Rs:../writableBox8PercentageThousandths on such a return refused it for a divisor that decides nothing. That divisor-UNANSWERED (or untied, or the box 9a procedure not running - present-but-unanswered counts) sub-population is what this arm frees, and it is the whole of what this arm frees. The divisor-ANSWERED-and-TIED sub-population was never refused HERE at all - it resolves ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies TRUE regardless of the election, because none of that fact's seven conjuncts tests the election, so the second arm carries it and always did.
WHY THE ARM CARRIES THREE CONJUNCTS AND NOT A BARE Not(../form4972TenYearElectionMade). (1)/(2) THE AMOUNT, complete and positive, the IsComplete before the value read as everywhere else here. The payer enters the percentage "along with the current actuarial value" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16), so a percentage with no amount is a payer contradiction. It cannot be caught one guard over either: ../box8OtherAmountUseIsUndetermined itself requires form1099Rs:../roundedOtherDollar greater than $0, so a percentage with no amount never reaches the VALUE guard, and without these two conjuncts it would go completely unrefused. (3) Not(../box8IsLongTermCareInvestmentReduction), which is the D1 landing review's BLOCKER repair carried up to this layer: a code W form whose charge is applied routes AWAY from line 11, so a bare election escape would let a payer-contradictory LTC form carrying a multiple-recipient percentage slip both this guard and the routing - the only return-level refusal of a non-zero box 8 percentage would go silent. The repair is stated on ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies for the mechanics gate; this fact restates it because the escape bypasses that gate.
WHAT THE ARM DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REPEAT: conjuncts (1), (3), (4) and (6) of ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies - divisor answered, divisor tied, divisor positive, box 9a procedure running. Those are exactly the requirements that are inert when Part III is not elected, and not repeating them is the entire content of the narrowing.
WHAT DOES NOT MOVE. A freed return does not thereby FILE. /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Value independently refuses every return carrying a positive box 8 amount that does not reach ../box8FilesOnForm4972, and ../box8FilesOnForm4972 requires ../form4972TenYearElectionMade - so on the whole freed population the VALUE guard still fires and /flowIsKnockedOut is unchanged. That is correct and is that contract's cell to relax or keep, not this one's.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the only value read is form1099Rs:../roundedOtherDollar and its IsComplete comes first; ../box8IsLongTermCareInvestmentReduction and ../form4972TenYearElectionMade are Switches with an else-False fall-through; and ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies is complete-safe by its own construction. On an unanswered box 8 the whole fact resolves FALSE, and the guard's own Count already excludes that item through form1099Rs:../causesRetirementBox8PercentageKO, so mid-intake posture is unchanged.

Fact.Name: Box 8 is the qualified long-term-care charge against the contract
Fact.Description: BOX 7 CODE W IS THE DISCRIMINATOR for the second of the payer's three uses of box 8. The payer instruction assigns that code to the long-term-care charge in as many words, Table 1 ties the code to IRC 72(e)(11) - the very provision that makes the charge a reduction in the investment in the contract rather than income - and box 2a is entered as zero for it. So a code W form's box 8 is NOT the current actuarial value of an annuity contract in a lump-sum distribution and must never reach Form 4972 line 11; this fact is what excludes it from ../box8RoutesToForm4972Line11. THE ROUTING, one unit after the classification: the charge reaches its statutory destination through ../box8LongTermCareChargeAgainstInvestment and ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract, and ../box8LongTermCareChargeIsApplied is the fact that says so. The PRIOR TEXT here read "the CLASSIFICATION lands here, the ROUTING does not. Nothing yet subtracts the charge from ../writableSimplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract, which is where 72(e)(11)(A) sends it" - true when written, stale now. MATCHED EXACTLY, like the two shipping code W tests in this module: a paired code (Table 1 pairs W with 6) is not matched and is a named gap.

Fact.Name: Box 8 long-term-care charge reducing the investment in the contract
Fact.Description: THE CLASSIFIED USE 2 AMOUNT, carried to the destination IRC 72(e)(11)(A) names. ../box8IsLongTermCareInvestmentReduction identifies a code W form's box 8 as the qualified long-term-care charge; this fact is that amount, and $0 on every other form. It is the subtrahend of BOTH halves of IRC 72(e)(11): ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract carries clause (A), the reduction in the investment, and ../simplifiedMethodIncludibleGrossDistribution carries clause (B), which keeps the same charge out of gross income even though the payer is instructed to report it inside box 1. It exists as its own fact so one amount serves both clauses and the classification and the amount stay separately readable.

Fact.Name: Investment in the contract after the box 8 long-term-care charge
Fact.Description: THE STATUTORY MINUEND, and the only thing this unit changed inside the Simplified Method. IRC 72(e)(11)(A) reduces the investment in the contract by the qualified long-term-care charge, "but not below zero", so this fact is the writable intake less ../box8LongTermCareChargeAgainstInvestment with a $0 floor. It equals the writable on every form that is not a code W form carrying a box 8 amount above $0, which is every form in the corpus. WHERE IT IS READ AND WHERE IT IS NOT: ../simplifiedMethodTaxableAmount reads it at both of its VALUE sites, the unrecovered-basis cap and the monthly exclusion. The IsComplete leg of ../simplifiedMethodInputsComplete deliberately still reads the WRITABLE: completeness is a property of what the filer answered, and this fact is Incomplete exactly when the writable is, so routing the leg through it would change no verdict and would only hide which intake is missing. A FINER READING THIS UNIT DID NOT ENCODE, named rather than silently taken. Pub. 575's Worksheet A line 2 is the cost "at the annuity starting date" and line 3 fixes the monthly exclusion from it, so a charge levied AFTER that date arguably reduces only the unrecovered balance and not the fixed monthly amount. No vendored line says which, and 72(e)(11)(A) reduces "the investment in the contract" without qualification, so the statute's unqualified minuend is what ships.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 1 after the box 8 long-term-care charge is excluded
Fact.Description: IRC 72(e)(11) HAS TWO CLAUSES AND THIS IS THE SECOND ONE. Clause (A) reduces the investment in the contract, which ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract does. Clause (B) says the charge "shall not be includible in gross income" - and without this fact the dictionary applied (A) alone, because the payer is INSTRUCTED to put the charge INSIDE box 1 ("Include in box 1 charges or payments for qualified long-term care insurance contracts under combined arrangements. Enter Code W in box 7"), and box 1 is what the Simplified Method subtracts the exclusion FROM. Applying (A) without (B) taxed the very charge the statute excludes. WHY THE MINUEND AND NOT A LATER SUBTRACTION, which is the shape the printed line supports. Pub. 575 Worksheet A line 1 is "Enter the total pension or annuity payments received this year", and a charge levied against the contract's cash value is not a payment received by the annuitant - the payer reports it in box 1 by instruction, not because the taxpayer received it. So the charge never belongs in line 1, and taking it out here keeps line 1, the line 9 taxable amount and Form 1040 line 5b consistent with one another. IT IS $0 AND THEREFORE INERT on every form that is not a code W form carrying a box 8 amount above $0, which is every form in the conformance corpus, so this fact equals form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/grossDistribution everywhere the corpus reaches. The $0 floor is defence in depth: the payer instruction already floors box 8 at zero, so a charge exceeding box 1 describes a non-compliant form rather than a real one. LINE 5a IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADJUSTED. This fact feeds the TAXABLE side only; the gross that reaches Form 1040 line 5a still comes from box 1 as the payer reported it, which is what every other reader of ../grossDistribution in this module already assumes.

Fact.Name: The box 8 long-term-care charge reached the investment in the contract
Fact.Description: THE CELL THIS UNIT FREED, stated as its own fact so the guard reads a claim rather than a conjunction. A code W form's box 8 charge stops being a refusal exactly when this return CARRIES it to the destination 72(e)(11)(A) names, which in this dictionary means the Simplified Method actually runs on this form: ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract is the only place the investment in the contract is consumed. COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, on the ../box8FilesOnForm4972 pattern - the IsComplete leg comes before the value leg, so a form whose box 2b or whose Worksheet A answers are still missing resolves FALSE and keeps refusing rather than degrading to a placeholder. BOTH CLAUSES OR NEITHER. "Applied" means clause (A) AND clause (B) have run, not just (A): the Simplified Method is the one computation here that reads the investment in the contract (A) and the one whose minuend contains the charge (B), so a single condition covers both. An earlier version of this unit gated on (A) alone and let the charge be taxed through box 1; the fixtures now pin the Form 1040 line 5b figure so that cannot recur silently. WHAT STILL REFUSES, and why it is not an "unsupported case": a code W form on which the Simplified Method does NOT run. The payer's own instruction enters $0 in box 2a for this charge, so the ordinary code W form has a DETERMINED taxable amount and no Worksheet A. On that return the charge is inert this year and reduces only a FUTURE year's basis, which this dictionary neither carries forward nor is told about by any vendored line. Treating it as inert would be exactly the unstated inference the eligible-but-not-electing cell was refused for, so it stays refused and the rebody names it.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 Part III ten-year option elected
Fact.Description: The Part III election alone, complete-safe. ../form4972InputsComplete accepts EITHER election, which is right for Form 4972 as a whole but wrong for box 8: Form 4972 line 11 is a Part III line, and a Part II capital-gain-only return computes no line 11 that does anything. Kept as its own fact so the box 8 filing cell can require Part III without changing ../form4972InputsComplete's legacy meaning for every other reader.

Fact.Name: Box 8 and the hand-entered Form 4972 line 11 disagree
Fact.Description: An input contradiction, refused rather than silently resolved. Form 4972 line 11 has two possible sources in this dictionary: the box 8 amount this unit routes, and the older hand-entered ../writableForm4972CurrentActuarialValue that existed because box 8 was unreachable. ../form4972Line11 PREFERS box 8, so a filer who answered the hand entry with a different non-zero figure would have it silently overridden and would never see which number the return used. That is the shape a refusal exists for. A zero hand entry is NOT a conflict - it is the printed instruction for the case with no annuity contract - and neither is an entry equal to the box 8 amount.

Fact.Name: Box 8 amount is this return's Form 4972 line 11
Fact.Description: THE ROUTING DECISION FOR BOX 8, and the reading it rests on. Form 4972 line 11 names box 8 by number, so the current actuarial value of an annuity contract included in a lump-sum distribution lands on Form 4972 line 11 and on no other line of the return: it is not in boxes 1 or 2a, and no instruction adds it to Form 1040 line 5a or 5b. THE ALTERNATIVE READING, and why it is not taken: IRC 72(c)(2) makes an actuarially computed refund-feature value a SUBTRACTION from the investment in the contract, which would change the tax-free part of later payments rather than adding anything this year (26 U.S.C. 72, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section72&num=0&edition=2024). That is a taxpayer-side exclusion-ratio adjustment, not the payer-reported figure box 8 carries: the payer instruction gives box 8 three uses, and none of them is the 72(c)(2) computation (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 16). Only the first of those three - the lump-sum annuity contract value - has a line on this return, so this fact is true only when the Form 4972 Part I eligibility gate is answered true, which is what keeps a long-term-care charge or an annuitized-contract year-end value out of line 11. A box 8 percentage turns it off: that case needs a gross-up division this dictionary cannot express.

Fact.Name: Box 8 amount carried to Form 4972 line 11
Fact.Description:
THE MULTIPLE-RECIPIENT GROSS-UP, residue item (i) of the kind="rebody" contract at form1099Rs:/knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage. The first Case is what stood here before; the new Case in front of it divides the box 8 amount by ../box8RecipientShareFraction when ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies, which is Form 4972's Step 2 box 8 bullet word for word: "Divide the amount from Form 1099-R, box 8, by the percentage in box 8. Enter the result on Form 4972, line 11."
OUTSIDE THE POPULATION NOTHING MOVES: ../box8MrdGrossUpApplies is complete-safe FALSE on every return that has not answered the numeric box 8 divisor, and no committed scenario answers it. THE ORDER OF THE CASES MATTERS: ../box8RoutesToForm4972Line11 is now true for a multiple-recipient share too, so the gross-up Case has to come first or the share would be carried to line 11 unscaled.

Fact.Name: Box 8 amount present with no routing this return can determine
Fact.Description: NAMED GAP, stated as a fact rather than left silent: a box 8 dollar amount above $0 that this return can neither route nor classify. It is the exact population form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/causesRetirementBox8ValueKO counts, and FIVE cells reach it. (1) USE 3 against USE 1 on a code that is not W - an annuitized commercial annuity contract's year-end value and a lump-sum annuity contract's current actuarial value are the two payer uses the form still gives no way to tell apart. (2) The form is Form 4972 eligible but elects NOTHING. (3) It elects Part II only: line 11 is a Part III line, so a capital-gain-only return computes no line that reads it. (4) The Form 4972 questions are still unanswered - a data-completeness cell, and the reason ../box8FilesOnForm4972 puts its IsComplete leg first. (5) The hand-entered ../writableForm4972CurrentActuarialValue disagrees with the routed box 8 amount (../box8ConflictsWithLegacyForm4972Line11). WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHY IT STILL REFUSES: a code W form. Its box 8 is the qualified long-term-care charge, which ../box8IsLongTermCareInvestmentReduction identifies from the code, so it is DETERMINED and does not belong in this fact. Whether it may FILE is a separate question ../box8RefusesThisReturn answers through ../box8LongTermCareChargeIsApplied: it files when this return actually carries the charge to the investment in the contract, and refuses when it does not. Measured, not assumed - code W is ALREADY a supported distribution code here, so nothing upstream refuses it.

Fact.Name: Box 8 still refuses this return
Fact.Description: THE UNION THE VALUE GUARD COUNTS, and it is two different refusals, not one. (i) ../box8OtherAmountUseIsUndetermined - the return cannot say WHERE the amount goes. (ii) a classified code W charge that this return has NOT carried to the investment in the contract - ../box8IsLongTermCareInvestmentReduction true with ../box8LongTermCareChargeIsApplied false. Leg (ii) used to be the bare classification, because nothing subtracted the charge from the investment in the contract. ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract now does, so a code W form whose Simplified Method runs FILES, and what leg (ii) still counts is the code W form on which no computation in this dictionary consumes the investment in the contract at all. Classified is not the same as computed, and only computed may file. WHY THIS FACT EXISTS AT ALL, measured rather than assumed: the review round that asked for the code W classification stated that code W returns are refused upstream by form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/hasUnsupportedDistributionCode. THEY ARE NOT. That fact reads ../hasSupportedDistributionCodeTreatment, which admits code W through ../supportedDistributionCodeTaxTreatment's own code W arm, so /knockoutForForm1099RDistributionCode resolves FALSE on a code W form - a code W long-term care charge is not refused. Excluding the classified cell from the guard on the strength of that premise would have let a code W return FILE with the statutory reduction silently dropped, overstating the tax-free part of every later Simplified Method payment.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 11
Fact.Description: Prefers the box 8 amount when it routes here, and otherwise keeps the hand-entered line 11 writable exactly as it resolved before box 8 was read - including its Incomplete state, which is what still gates Part III through ../form4972InputsComplete.

Fact.Name: Box 8 is routed to a Form 4972 this return actually computes
Fact.Description: The condition under which a box 8 amount stops being a refusal. Routing alone is not enough: Form 4972 line 11 only exists on a return that files a Form 4972, so this fact also requires the Part I eligibility and the Part II or Part III election that ../form4972InputsComplete measures. COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the IsComplete leg comes before the value leg, so a return whose Form 4972 questions are unanswered resolves FALSE rather than Incomplete, and the guard that reads it keeps refusing mid-intake instead of degrading to a placeholder.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 21
Fact.Description: Line 16 multiplied by the line 20 decimal. THE LINE 20 DECIMAL IS NOT MATERIALIZED AS A FACT, and that is the point of this node. The form prints line 20 as line 11 divided by line 12 "rounded to at least three places" - a FLOOR, not a scale. This fact graph has no decimal type that meets it: a Dollar carries two places, which is BELOW the printed floor, and a Rational is exact but cannot be constructed from two Dollar operands. Dividing first and multiplying second therefore lost precision - the shipping body computed 3000/13000 as 0.23 and put $1,495.00 here instead of $1,500.00. Multiplying first and dividing last carries the exact ratio, which is the limit the floor permits and is never less accurate than three places.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 7
Fact.Description:
Form 4972 line 7, which the form states as "Multiply line 6 by 20% (0.20)". It now multiplies LINE 6 (../form4972Line6), which is what the printed line says, instead of recomputing 20 percent of Form 1099-R box 3 (../capitalGain) on its own.
WHY THAT MATTERS. Until this edit the two Part II lines read DIFFERENT quantities that happened to be equal: line 6 carried box 3 and line 7 carried a fifth of box 3. They stop being equal the moment line 6 takes a worksheet result instead of box 3, which it now does on a return that takes the death benefit exclusion (the Death Benefit Worksheet's line F is routed "here and on Form 4972, line 6"). Re pointing line 7 at line 6 is what makes the correction on line 6 reach the tax: line 7 feeds ../lumpSumDistributionForm4972Tax directly, so a beneficiary taking the exclusion was taxed on 20 percent of the UNREDUCED capital gain part.
BYTE IDENTICAL WHERE LINE 6 STILL CARRIES BOX 3, which is every committed return: line 6 is box 3 under the capital gain election and $0 without it, so Round(1/5 x line 6) is the expression that stood here, term for term, and the completeness is the same because line 6 switches on the same election intake.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 8, the ordinary-income addend, before any box 9a division
Fact.Description: The first of line 8's two addends, materialised so that residue item (ii) of the rebody at /knockoutForForm1099RBox9aPercentage can divide BOTH of them without restating either expression. BYTE-FOR-BYTE the expression that stood inside ../form4972Line8's Add before that date: the capital-gain election takes box 2a minus box 3 floored at zero, and every other return takes box 2a.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 8, the net unrealized appreciation addend, before any box 9a division
Fact.Description: The second of line 8's two addends, materialised alongside the first and BYTE-FOR-BYTE the expression that stood inside ../form4972Line8's Add before that date: box 6 when the NUA election is answered and made, and $0 otherwise, with the IsComplete leg first so an unanswered election resolves $0 rather than Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 8, the net unrealized appreciation term actually entered
Fact.Description:
The NUA amount that Step 3 of the multiple recipient / NUA instructions puts INTO line 8, as opposed to ../form4972Line8NuaAddend, which is box 6 whole and is the NUA Worksheet's LINE D, closing the gap ../form4972Line8's own Description names.
THE TWO STEP 3 BULLETS ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS, and the form is explicit about it. "If you aren't making the capital gain election, add the amount from Form 1099-R, box 2a, to the amount in box 6" — box 6 whole, which is ../form4972Line8NuaAddend. "If you are making the capital gain election, subtract the amount from Form 1099-R, box 3, from the amount in box 2a. Add to the result the amount from line F of your NUA Worksheet" — line F, the ORDINARY INCOME portion of NUA, because the capital gain portion (worksheet line E) has already gone to line 6 through worksheet line G. Adding box 6 whole there taxes the capital gain portion of the NUA twice, once at the 20 percent Part II rate and again inside the Part III ten year table.
NO CYCLE, and the reason to read this Description before editing either fact: the NUA Worksheet's line D IS ../form4972Line8NuaAddend, and ../form4972NuaWorksheetLineF is line D minus line E. So line F depends on the addend; this term depends on line F; and nothing depends back. The correction had to land as a NEW fact between them rather than as an edit to the addend, which would have made the worksheet depend on its own output.
BYTE IDENTICAL UNLESS BOTH ELECTIONS ARE MADE: without the capital gain election this is the addend unchanged, and without the NUA election both arms are $0. No committed scenario makes both elections.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 8
Fact.Description:
RESIDUE ITEM (ii) OF THE REBODY AT /knockoutForForm1099RBox9aPercentage. On a multiple-recipient lump sum this line is not this recipient's share - it is the WHOLE lump sum, which is the only way the progressive ten-year table on lines 23 through 28 can be applied before Step 5 takes the share back out on line 29.
BOTH ADDENDS DIVIDE, and the contract said so for a reason: Form 4972's Step 2 divides box 2a (or box 2a minus box 3, on the capital-gain election) by the box 9a percentage, and Step 3's NUA bullets divide box 2a PLUS box 6 by the same percentage. Dividing each addend by the same divisor and adding is the same number as dividing their sum, so the two Divides here are the printed instruction and not an approximation of it.
OUTSIDE THE POPULATION NOTHING MOVES: ../box9aMrdDivisionApplies is complete-safe FALSE on every return that has not answered the numeric divisor, and the second Case is the Add that stood here before this unit, over the same two expressions now carrying their own names.
THAT NAMED GAP IS CLOSED. What stood here said Step 3's capital-gain-plus-NUA bullet (lines 179-191, RIGHT column) divides box 2a minus box 3 PLUS "the amount from line F of your NUA Worksheet", and that ../form4972Line8NuaAddend carried box 6 whole instead. The NUA Worksheet has since been modelled, so the second addend of both arms is now ../form4972Line8NuaTerm, which is worksheet line F under the capital gain election and the box 6 addend without it. Read that fact's Description before touching either: line F's own line D IS the addend, so the term had to be a new fact rather than an edit to the addend. Byte identical unless BOTH elections are made, which no committed scenario does.

Form 4972 line 16, "Minimum distribution allowance. Subtract line 15 from line 13": the difference of the two printed lines, each already rounded to whole dollars (../form4972Line13 and ../form4972Line15), so the printed lines 13, 15 and 16 subtract exactly. Both are $0 when line 12 is $70,000 or more, which is the printed skip to line 17. Floored at $0.

Fact.Name: Form 4972 Part I eligibility, born-before-1936 test admits the line 3 beneficiary route
Fact.Description: Form 4972 Part I line 4 bars the form unless the RECIPIENT was born before January 2, 1936; line 3 admits a SEPARATE population, "paid to you as a beneficiary of a plan participant who was born before" that date, and the printed instruction after line 4 reads the two together: "If you answered 'No' to both questions 3 and 4, don't use this form." Before this correction the first conjunct read only form1099Rs:../dateOfBirthBefore1936 (the recipient's own line 4 test), so a beneficiary filing on a pre-1936 participant's plan under line 3 could never make this fact resolve true no matter how the remaining Part I/II/III answers came in. The fix admits either route: the recipient's own line 4 birth date, OR a Yes answer to ../writableForm4972Part1PaidAsBeneficiaryOfParticipantBornBefore1936 (line 3). COMPLETE-SAFE ON THE NEW DISJUNCT: the IsComplete leg comes before the value read, so an unanswered line 3 resolves the disjunct false rather than incomplete, exactly the pattern the sibling facts in this module use throughout. Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 25 minus line 28, before the multiple-recipient share is taken

Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 29

Multiple recipients, see instructions", and the instructions it points at are Step 5's worksheet: A is line 25 minus line 28, B is "your percentage of the distribution from box 9a", and C is "Multiply line A by line B. Enter here and on Form 4972, line 29. Also, write MRD on the dotted line next to line 29".
THIS IS WHERE THE SHARE COMES BACK OUT. ../form4972Line8 grossed the recipient's share up to the whole lump sum so the progressive ten-year table could be applied to it; without this multiply-back the return would pay ten-year tax on somebody else's money as well as its own. Fact.Name: Form 4972 line 30 tax
Box 10 amount excepted from recapture
Box 10 recapture amount included on Form 5329 line 1

Fact.Name: Box 7 reports an early distribution from a Roth IRA
Fact.Description: TRUE when box 7 on this Form 1099-R is code J, or the JS pair in either payer order. Code J is the payer's statement that the distribution came from a Roth IRA or a Roth SIMPLE IRA and that no exception is known; the JS pair is the Roth SIMPLE IRA inside its first 2 years, which is still a Roth IRA distribution. Incomplete while box 7 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Box 7 reports a distribution from a Roth IRA of any kind
Fact.Description: TRUE when box 7 is J, JS or SJ (an early Roth IRA distribution), J with 8 or P in either payer order (a corrective distribution out of a Roth IRA), Q (a qualified Roth IRA distribution) or T (a Roth IRA distribution where the payer does not know whether the 5-year period is met). Q and T take no pairs. Code J is the payer's statement that the money came out of a Roth IRA whatever its companion code, and Table 1 lets J stand beside 8, P or S, so every one of those pairs is a Roth IRA form. The J8, 8J, JP and PJ pairs are added here and NOT to ../isRothIraEarlyDistribution, whose readers carry the Form 5329 line 1 conversion recapture: a corrective return of an excess Roth IRA contribution is not the early distribution that recapture is allocated to. A Roth IRA is taxed under IRC 408A(d) and its distributions are NOT the section 408(d)(1) withdrawals Form 5329 line 11 asks for, so this is the exclusion that keeps a Roth distribution out of the traditional IRA offset even when the payer ticks the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box. Fact.Name: Box 7 reports an early distribution from a SIMPLE IRA in its first 2 years
Fact.Description: TRUE when box 7 on this Form 1099-R is code S, or the JS pair in either payer order. Fact.Name: This Form 1099-R is a traditional, SEP or SIMPLE IRA distribution that Form 8606 Part I describes
Fact.Description: True when the form is an IRA form (the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is checked, or box 7 carries an 8/J or 8/K pair that marks IRA assets without the box) and box 7 is not known to be a Roth IRA code. Fact.Name: The part of this IRA Form 1099-R that Form 8606 line 7 or line 8 must hold
Fact.Description: For a traditional, SEP or SIMPLE IRA form (../isTraditionalIraForm8606Item), box 1 less what line 7 leaves out and this return already computes on its own: a supported qualified charitable distribution (form1099Rs:../line4cQcdExclusion), a supported HSA funding distribution (form1099Rs:../line4cHfdExclusion), and the part of an elected direct rollover that was rolled over (box 1 less box 2a). $0 on any other form. An exclusion that cannot yet be read counts as $0, so an unfinished line 4c answer can only make this larger, which errs toward refusal. Never below $0.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's traditional IRA Form 1099-R box 1 total
Fact.Description: ../form8606Line7Share (the path is /form1099Rs/*/form8606Line7Share: box 1 less any supported QCD, HFD and elected direct rollover) summed over the primary filer's Form 1099-Rs that ../isTraditionalIraForm8606Item marks (the path is /form1099Rs/*/isTraditionalIraForm8606Item). Fact.Name: The traditional IRA Form 1099-R box 1 total that is not the primary filer's
Fact.Description: ../form8606Line7Share (the path is /form1099Rs/*/form8606Line7Share: box 1 less any supported QCD, HFD and elected direct rollover) summed over every traditional IRA Form 1099-R that is not known to be the primary filer's: the spouse's forms, and any form whose owner is still unanswered, which therefore has to be covered by the spouse's Form 8606 before the Form 8606 route can carry the return. $0 on a return with no such form; Incomplete while a counted form's box 1 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: The Form 8606 route of Form 1040 line 4b carries every IRA Form 1099-R on the return
Fact.Description: Form 1040 line 4b takes the Form 8606 result in place of the Form 1099-R collection as soon as either spouse claims Form 8606 Part I, and it then reads no Form 1099-R amount at all. This fact is true only when that replacement drops nothing. Three conditions. (1) Each owner who has traditional IRA Form 1099-Rs claims a complete Form 8606 whose lines 7 and 8 together are at least the box 1 total of that owner's forms; a spouse's forms need a joint return and the spouse's own Form 8606. (2) A form whose owner is unanswered is held to the spouse's Form 8606 and so refuses on a return without one. Each form counts at box 1 less the supported QCD, HFD and elected direct rollover this return already computes (/form1099Rs/*/form8606Line7Share); a returned contribution or an indirect rollover is not netted out, so such a form refuses rather than files: the error runs toward refusal, never toward a smaller line 4b. Fact.Description: True when either spouse claims Form 8606 Part I beside at least one IRA Form 1099-R and the Form 8606 amounts, once entered, do not carry every such form: an owner with traditional IRA forms whose Form 8606 is not claimed, or whose lines 7 and 8 fall short of that owner's forms (/primaryFilerTraditionalIraForm1099RGrossForForm8606, /secondaryFilerTraditionalIraForm1099RGrossForForm8606); the spouse's forms on a return that is not a joint return; or a Roth IRA form with a box 2a amount above $0 (form8606:/form8606RothForm1099RWithTaxableAmount), which Part I does not carry. It reads only answered amounts: while a compared Form 8606 amount is still blank it stays false, and the return is incomplete for that reason instead.

Fact.Name: Form 8606 figures this IRA Form 1099-R's line 4b amount
Fact.Description: True when this Form 1099-R is a traditional, SEP or SIMPLE IRA form (../isTraditionalIraForm8606Item), at least one spouse claims Form 8606 Part I, so the Form 8606 arm is the one Form 1040 line 4b takes, and that arm carries every IRA Form 1099-R on the return (/form8606CoversEveryIraForm1099R). On such a form box 2a is not the taxable amount and box 2b is usually checked, because the payer does not know the owner's basis; Form 8606 is what figures it. A refusal that holds a box 2b form until its taxable amount is figured can stand down on this fact. False on a Roth IRA form, on a return without Form 8606, and whenever the Form 8606 amounts fall short of the IRA forms.

Fact.Name: What this Form 1099-R puts on Form 5329 line 1 when its box 7 code is an early-distribution code
Fact.Description:
The includible part of this distribution, which is what Form 5329 line 1 takes for an early distribution. Every reader tests the early-distribution code set (form1099Rs:../flowQualifiedEarlyDistribution) first; this fact only says how much.
ON THE FORM 8606 ROUTE (../form8606FiguresThisIraItem Complete true) box 2a is not the taxable amount: the owner's Form 8606 figures it, and only the part left after basis recovery is includible. The item takes its pro rata share of its owner's includible line 7 amount: ../form8606Line7Share times the owner's line 15a less the Line 15c Worksheet repayment reduction (form8606:/form8606Line15aLessRepaymentReduction, or form8606:/spouseForm8606Line15aLessRepaymentReduction), divided by the owner's line 7 (form8606:/writableForm8606Distributions, or the spouse's). Pro rata because all of an owner's traditional IRAs are one contract and the year's distributions one distribution, so every distribution carries the same nontaxable fraction. The owner is the primary filer when form1099Rs:../belongsToPrimaryFiler is Complete true and the secondary filer otherwise, the same split /form8606CoversEveryIraForm1099R uses. Capped at form1099Rs:../line4bTaxableAmount, so the Form 8606 route never puts more on line 1 than the form itself would. $0 when the owner's line 7 is not above $0: such an item can only be a conversion, which is on line 8 and is not subject to the additional tax. The qualified disaster portion is not taken out here; Form 5329 takes the qualified disaster recovery distributions off line 1 itself.
OTHERWISE form1099Rs:../line4bTaxableAmount (box 2a less any QCD and HFD exclusion), which is what line 1 took before this fact existed. That includes an item whose Form 8606 question is still open (../form8606FiguresThisIraItem not Complete).

Fact.Name: This form's Form 4972 Part III ten-year tax is actually computed
Fact.Description:
THE CONDITION UNDER WHICH A PART III FIGURE REACHES THE RETURN, isolated as its own fact so a guard can read it without inheriting any other reader's meaning. ../form4972TenYearElectionMade is the election alone; this fact is the election AND the inputs ../lumpSumDistributionForm4972Tax needs before it computes anything but $0. Both halves are load-bearing: that fact's own Switch answers a hard $0 when ../form4972InputsComplete is false, so nothing is at stake on a return that answered the election but is not eligible; and a return that elected Part II only computes no line 8 and no line 29, so its Part III lines are not at stake either.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, on the ../box8FilesOnForm4972 pattern: the IsComplete leg comes before the value leg, so a mid-intake return resolves FALSE rather than Incomplete and a guard reading it keeps its own completeness instead of degrading to a placeholder.

Fact.Name: Box 9a percentage as a number, in percent units
Fact.Description:
form1099Rs:../writableBox9aPercentageThousandths divided by 1000. 50000 becomes the Rational 50, which is 50 PERCENT and not the fraction one half - ../box9aRecipientShareFraction is the fraction. Kept in percent units here because that is the unit the MeF String is written in, and the tie in ../box9aDivisorTiesToMefString compares the two spellings of the same number.
INCOMPLETE when the intake is unanswered, deliberately: every reader goes through ../box9aMrdDivisionApplies, which is complete-safe.

Fact.Name: The numeric box 9a divisor is the same number the MeF String says
Fact.Description:
THE TIE residue item (i) of the rebody at /knockoutForForm1099RBox9aPercentage requires: a second, numeric intake for a box the payer already reported as a String must not be able to disagree with it. The Match limit on form1099Rs:../writablePercentageTotalDistribution admits exactly four spellings of any one percentage - "50", "50.0", "50.00", "50.000" - so the test is an Any over those four.
THE TIE IS EXACT AND TWO-WAY, which the contract's own four-scale Any was not. That version compared the String to AsDecimalString of the Rational at scales 0 through 3, and AsDecimalString's setScale is HALF_UP, so a divisor of 50.4 renders "50" at scale 0 and matched a String that said 50. Here the comparison runs the other way round: the divisor is rendered ONCE at scale 3 - exact, because ../box9aPercentageAsRational is an integer number of thousandths over 1000 and has nothing to round - and each arm pads the String out to the same three decimal places before comparing. Only one arm can match a given String, since the four padded forms have four different lengths.
A SPELLING THAT TIES FALSE ON PURPOSE: a leading zero. "05" is not one of the four renderings AsDecimalString produces for 5 - those are "5", "5.0", "5.00", "5.000" - so a String written "05" never matches any arm however correct the numeric divisor is, and the return REFUSES. That is the safe direction and it costs nothing: the MeF RatioType Match limit is what a payer's percentage must already satisfy, and normalising the String is the application's job, not a place for the engine to guess that two spellings mean one number.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, on the ../box8FilesOnForm4972 pattern: both IsComplete legs come before any value read, so a return that has answered neither box resolves FALSE rather than Incomplete and the guard that reads it keeps its own completeness.

Fact.Name: Box 9a percentage as the fraction Form 4972 divides by and multiplies back
Fact.Description: ../box9aPercentageAsRational over 100. 50 percent becomes the Rational one half, which is the operand Form 4972's Step 2 divides box 2a by and Step 5 multiplies (line 25 minus line 28) by. INCOMPLETE when the intake is unanswered; every reader goes through ../box9aMrdDivisionApplies.

Fact.Name: This form's Form 4972 figures are scaled by the box 9a percentage
Fact.Description:
THE POPULATION GATE for the whole multiple-recipient procedure, isolated so that every division and the line 29 multiply-back read ONE condition and no reader has to restate it. Four conjuncts, in this order and for these reasons.
(1) IsComplete on form1099Rs:../writableBox9aPercentageThousandths, first, so that a return that has not answered the numeric intake resolves FALSE here rather than dragging Incomplete into Form 4972 line 8. (2) form1099Rs:../causesRetirementBox9aPercentageKO, which is TRUE exactly when the MeF String is answered and has a character outside "0." - a box 9a of "0" or "0.000" is not a share and is not counted, which is also why nothing here can divide by zero through that door. (3) ../box9aDivisorTiesToMefString, so a divisor that contradicts the transmitted String scales nothing. (4) a literal GreaterThan zero on the intake, which conjunct (2) already implies through the tie but which is stated anyway, because "no Divide in this module can see a zero divisor" should be readable at the division site and not reconstructed from two other facts.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the IsComplete leg comes before every value read, and both facts it reads are themselves complete-safe.

Fact.Name: A positive Form 4972 line 11 on a box 9a return whose line 10 has been grossed up
Fact.Description:
RESIDUE ITEM (iv) OF THE REBODY AT /knockoutForForm1099RBox9aPercentage, landed in the same commit as the guard widening, because the contract says it "is not owed until (ii) lands, but it is owed then".
THE CONTRADICTION. Form 4972's multiple-recipient procedure divides TWO boxes by TWO different percentages in the same step: box 2a by the box 9a percentage onto line 8, and box 8 by the BOX 8 percentage onto line 11. Line 12 adds line 10 (which carries the grossed-up line 8) to line 11. A form that reports a box 8 AMOUNT and a box 9a percentage but NO box 8 percentage therefore makes line 12 the sum of a whole-lump-sum figure and one recipient's share of an annuity contract - two different scales in one addition, and the ten-year table is applied to the total.
WHY REFUSING IS THE HONEST ANSWER RATHER THAN PICKING A DIVISOR. The payer instructions say the box 8 percentage is REQUIRED in this situation: "If an annuity contract is part of a multiple recipient lump-sum distribution, enter in box 8, along with the current actuarial value, the percentage of the total annuity contract each Form 1099-R represents". So the combination is a payer contradiction, and nothing on the return says whether the box 8 percentage was omitted or the box 9a percentage was entered in error. Guessing which box is short would put a number on the return that no source supports.
THE TEST IS LINE 11 ITSELF, NOT THE BOX 8 AMOUNT, and that is a correction made in this unit's own review round. ../form4972Line11 has TWO sources - ../box8CurrentActuarialValueForForm4972 when box 8 routes there, and the hand-entered ../writableForm4972CurrentActuarialValue otherwise - and NEITHER is scaled by anything. Testing the box 8 amount alone left the second source open: a box-9a Part III return with no box 8 at all but a hand-entered line 11 of $3,000 filed with line 10 at whole-lump-sum scale and line 11 at its own, the identical $63,000 line 12 this fact exists to refuse, and it had REFUSED before this unit widened the guard. THE WITHDRAWN REASONING, quoted rather than deleted: "the taxpayer entering line 11 directly is entering the figure Step 2's bullet would have produced, already divided". The printed form argues the other way - line 11 reads "Current actuarial value of annuity from Form 1099-R, box 8. If none, enter -0-" (f4972 line 40), so the hand entry is a stand-in for BOX 8, at box 8's own scale, and nothing on the return says whether the filer divided it. Refusing is the honest answer for the same reason it is for box 8 itself.
WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REFUSE, so that silence is not read as coverage. A NON-ZERO box 8 percentage does not come here at all - /knockoutForForm1099RBox8Percentage already refuses that return on its own footing, and ../box8IsMultipleRecipientShare is the same string test that guard uses. THE PATH NAME records the shape that motivated this fact rather than its final scope; it is registered in dictionary/targets.json and is deliberately not renamed.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the IsComplete leg on the box 8 amount comes before its value read, and the other three conjuncts are complete-safe facts.

Fact.Name: Box 9a percentage this return can carry without misstating a figure
Fact.Description:
TWO DIFFERENT CONSISTENCIES, and this fact carries both.
(1) THE PAYER-SIDE ONE, unchanged and still the first three conjuncts. Box 9a is the percentage of a TOTAL distribution paid to the recipient named on this form, so a percentage on a form not marked total distribution, on an IRA/SEP/SIMPLE form, or on a direct rollover contradicts itself, and no computation can decide which box is wrong.
(2) THE RETURN-SIDE ONE, ADDED BY, because an internally consistent box 9a percentage still has an arithmetic consequence this dictionary does not compute. Form 4972's multiple-recipient procedure divides Form 1099-R box 2a by the box 9a percentage onto line 8 (Step 2, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4972.pdf, page 3, the MIDDLE column of a three-column page) and multiplies (line 25 minus line 28) by the same percentage onto line 29, marked "MRD" (Step 5, lines 202-213, the RIGHT column). ../form4972Line8 performs NO division and no line 29 fact exists anywhere in this module, so a Part III election on a box-9a form taxes this recipient's SHARE as if it were the whole lump sum, on a progressive ten-year table, with nothing scaling the result back down. THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR IS IRS-ADVERSE: for example, a $30,000 half share filed a $2,520.00 Part III tax where the printed procedure computes $3,835.00. The divisor cannot be supplied here - the intake is a Writable String carrying the MeF RatioType Match limit and the compnode set holds no string-to-number operator - so the return REFUSES instead of understating.
THE THREE SENTENCES ABOVE NO LONGER DESCRIBE WHAT THIS DICTIONARY DOES. ../form4972Line8 DOES divide - both of its addends - and line 29 IS a fact, ../form4972Line29, which multiplies the share back in. The divisor IS supplied here: not by converting the String, which is still impossible, but by a second numeric intake, form1099Rs:../writableBox9aPercentageThousandths, tied to the String by ../box9aDivisorTiesToMefString. So the fourth conjunct below is no longer Not(../form4972PartIIITaxIsComputed): a Part III box-9a return now FILES when the divisor is answered, ties and is positive and there is no box 8 contradiction, and REFUSES otherwise. The $3,835.00 the paragraph above computes by hand is now the figure the engine computes. The sole-recipient over-refusal (box 9a = 100) closes with no special case, since 100 divides by 1.
WHY THE PART II ELECTION IS NOT NARROWED WITH IT. Step 1 of the same procedure is "Complete Form 4972, Parts I and II" (line 179, MIDDLE column) and contains no division at all. Part II reads line 6 from box 3, which the payer already reports as this recipient's own share, and line 7 is 20 percent of that. Nothing in Part II is scaled by box 9a, so a capital-gain-only election on a box-9a form keeps filing.
WHAT THIS NARROWING ALSO MOVES, disclosed rather than left to be found: ../box9aShareOfTotalDistribution reads this fact, so on a refused return it resolves $0.00 instead of the gross distribution. It has no reader in this dictionary - it is an Export downstreamFacts value only - and the return does not file, but the exported value changes and that is stated here rather than anywhere else.

Fact.Name: Amount reported to this recipient when box 9a is present
Box 7 carries a two-code combination Table 1's used-with columns support
Fact.Description: Removed five pairs Table 1 does not support. BK and KB: code B's own used-with column is "1, 2, 4, 7, 8, G, L, M, P, or U" (no K), and code K's own column is "1, 2, 4, 7, 8, G, or Y" (no B) -- https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099r--2025.pdf, page 19 (B) and 1286-1297 (K). 4Y, 7Y and KY: code Y's own row states "When using code Y, you must use either 4, 7, or K" and its footnote is explicit about order -- "When reporting a QCD, you must use code Y FIRST with either 4, 7, or K" (line 1341) -- so the lawful forms are Y4, Y7 and YK (Y first, kept below, unchanged) and 4Y/7Y/KY (Y second) are the same digits in the wrong order. Fact.Description: Code 8 means excess contributions plus earnings or excess deferrals taxable in TY2025. A payer may also report it in a lawful Table 1 pair; test for the code digit only after the pair has been validated, so a malformed pairing cannot acquire the line-1h treatment. Fact.Description: Codes J and K identify Roth IRA distributions and traditional IRA assets. Fact.Name: Contract acquired for valuable consideration
Fact.Description:

IT IS ONLY REACHABLE OFF A NON-REPORTABLE-POLICY-SALE ANSWER. IRC 101(a)(3)(A) switches the entire second sentence off for a reportable policy sale, so on the attested arm this question is irrelevant BY STATUTE and ../reportableDeathBenefitIsAttested never reads it.

(2) CARRYOVER BASIS - 101(a)(2)(A), the first carve-out in the paragraph's second sentence. (3) TRANSFER TO THE INSURED OR A RELATED PARTY - 101(a)(2)(B), the second.

Fact.Name: Taxable amount of a reportable death benefit (IRC 6050Y) paid under a life insurance contract
Fact.Description:
THE INCLUDIBLE PART OF AN ATTESTED REPORTABLE DEATH BENEFIT: box 1 less the consideration and premiums the filer paid, floored at zero.
THE STATUTE, in the order it applies. IRC 101(a)(1) excludes death proceeds in full. 101(a)(2) FIRST sentence caps that exclusion at "the sum of the actual value of such consideration and the premiums and other amounts subsequently paid by the transferee" for a transfer for valuable consideration. Its SECOND sentence would carve two classes of transfer back OUT of the cap - carryover basis, and a transfer to the insured or the insured's partner, partnership or corporation. AND 101(a)(3)(A) SWITCHES THAT SECOND SENTENCE OFF for a reportable policy sale. So on the attested arm the cap applies UNCONDITIONALLY and the two carve-outs are irrelevant BY STATUTE - which is the whole reason this arm can be computed without modelling them.
THE ARITHMETIC IS THE INCLUSION, NOT THE EXCLUSION. The excluded amount is the LESSER of the payment and the sum; the includible amount is therefore the payment less the sum, and never below zero, because an exclusion capped at more than the payment simply excludes all of it. GreaterOf is that floor, and it is why a basis above box 1 gives $0 rather than a negative pension line.
WHAT IS NOT BUILT, and it is named rather than silent. The NON-reportable-policy-sale transfer for value - 101(a)(2) with its second sentence live - needs both carve-outs modelled and is NOT computed here; that form stays refused.

What still refuses on this guard is arm (2), box 13 on a code 4 form, and the unanswered intake; the rebody contract names both.
ARM (2) IS DISCHARGED. A code 4, 4D or D4 form whose filer answers ../writableBox1IsTheDeathBenefitUnderThatContract TRUE now reaches BOTH Case families above - the attested one and the non-sale one - and NOTHING IN THIS SWITCH CHANGED to admit it. What still refuses on this guard is the unanswered intake (arm (3)), a code 4 form paired with a companion code other than D, and a per-form attestation answered NO.

Fact.Description: True when the filer answered Yes to ../writableSimplifiedMethodSimultaneousAnnuitants AND this form's taxable amount is figured by the Simplified Method (../simplifiedMethodInputsComplete is Complete and true, on either the manual or the calculated worksheet). The pro rata share of the monthly tax-free amount is not computed, so the whole exclusion would otherwise be taken. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: every completeness test comes first in its conjunction, so an unanswered question, a No, a form held on an unanswered worksheet input and every form not on the Simplified Method all read false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Simplified Method pension shared with a simultaneous annuitant
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when at least one Form 1099-R whose taxable amount comes from the Simplified Method belongs to an annuity under which the filer and another annuitant are paid at the same time. Each such annuitant excludes only a pro rata share of the monthly tax-free amount (the filer's monthly payment over the total monthly payments to all annuitants), and this return does not ask the total paid to the others, so it would exclude the whole amount and understate the taxable pension on Form 1040 line 5b. SCREEN: "You told us that you and another person are paid under the same pension or annuity at the same time. In that case the tax-free part of each payment must be shared between you, and this return cannot figure your share yet, so it cannot be filed here." COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on a return with no Form 1099-R, or with the Form 1099-R list unanswered, and on every return where no form is a Simplified Method form answered Yes.

Fact.Name: Carry line 4 from the 2024 Simplified Method worksheet
Fact.Description: True if this annuity began before 2025 and a correctly prepared 2024 worksheet was used. Carry that worksheet monthly exclusion; skip the divisor and age-table computation even if the pension changed. False means line 4 must be computed from original cost and the original-start-age table or fixed contract count. Answer false for a 2025 start. Historical recovery and legal method eligibility are still required.

Fact.Name: 2024 Worksheet A line 4 monthly exclusion
Fact.Description: Unchanged monthly tax-free amount from the correct 2024 worksheet, including any already-required original adjustments. Supply only on the carry branch. It is NOT the annual exclusion, remaining cost, box 5 amount, or a newly calculated value based on current age. This bounded route has no simultaneous-beneficiary allocation or intervening investment change.

Fact.Name: Original primary annuitant age at the annuity starting date
Fact.Description: Whole years of age of the original primary annuitant on the legally determined original starting date, including when the current recipient is the sequential survivor. Never substitute current age or automatically use the recipient date of birth. Required for a fresh calculation, including the age-75 test on fixed-period contracts. The prior-year line-4 carry branch does not require this skipped table input.

Fact.Name: Sole survivor annuitant age at the original starting date
Fact.Description: Whole years of age of the sole eligible sequential survivor annuitant at the ORIGINAL annuity starting date. Used only for a fresh multiple-lives annuity starting in 1998 or later. Do not use current age, add other beneficiaries or include an entitlement dependent on a condition other than the primary death. The no-primary and multi-survivor populations remain outside this source-confirmed route.

Fact.Name: Entitled to fewer than five years of guaranteed payments at commencement
Fact.Description: Required on the fresh calculation only when the original primary annuitant was at least 75. True means the contract guarantees LESS than five years, using Pub. 575 definition including minimum guaranteed amounts and ignoring increases; exactly five years is false. A period-certain feature of a life annuity is not by itself a fixed-period annuity classification.

Fact.Name: Original number of monthly fixed-period contract payments
Fact.Description: Original count of at least thirteen monthly payments under a fixed-period annuity not dependent in whole or part on any life. Not the remaining number and not the current-year months. Life annuities with a fixed-period feature use the appropriate life table instead. The actual arrangement must span more than one full year; at least thirteen monthly payments is necessary but not by itself proof of that duration. Required only for a fresh fixed-period calculation; a pre-November-19-1996 fixed-period annuity cannot enter this Simplified Method route.

Fact.Name: Valid Simplified Method choice for the older life annuity
Fact.Description: For a life annuity starting after July 1, 1986 and before November 19, 1996, confirm the Simplified Method was validly chosen and has been continued. This is historical evidence, not an election now. A false or missing answer cannot switch a prior General Rule annuity to this method.

Fact.Name: Explicit Simplified Method worksheet selected
Fact.Description: Complete-safe optional worksheet request; false when its new request input is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Supported Simplified Method date and annuity type
Fact.Description: Starting date must be after July 1, 1986 and within calendar 2025 or earlier. Life annuities before November 19, 1996 need the historical choice separately. Fixed-period contracts before that date require the General Rule and are excluded. Unknown type/date is not defaulted.

Fact.Name: Older-annuity method selection verified
Fact.Description: Require the historical Simplified Method choice for pre-November-19-1996 annuities; later starts require no such input.

Fact.Name: Simplified Method age or guarantee condition for the selected worksheet
Fact.Description: For a fresh calculation, under age 75 qualifies; age 75 or older requires fewer than five guaranteed years. On a 2024-line-4 carry, use the existing attested original eligibility rather than inventing an age or asking skipped table inputs. Qualification is separate from the expected-payment count.

Fact.Name: Legacy age-or-guarantee answer agrees
Fact.Description: A supplied legacy condition must agree with the fresh original-age determination. On the carry branch that legacy condition is itself the required input. Omission on a fresh calculation is allowed; contradiction is not.

Fact.Name: Combined original ages for Table 2
Fact.Description: Add only the original primary and sole sequential survivor ages, with nonnegative inputs. This amount is neither a sum of current ages nor a household age.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 3 calculated from original ages or contract
Fact.Description: Table 1 covers single life and multiple lives starting before 1998. Its columns change on November 19, 1996. Later multiple-life annuities use Table 2 and combined original ages. Fixed-period contracts use their original monthly count only within the source-confirmed more-than-one-full-year arrangement; twelve or fewer original monthly payments are not eligible for this periodic route. The prior-year line-4 carry SKIPS this result (Incomplete/not applicable); no changed age or manual divisor replaces a historical monthly exclusion.

Fact.Name: Manual divisor agrees with the calculated line 3
Fact.Description: On a fresh worksheet a supplied manual divisor must match the age-derived or fixed-contract value exactly, not merely occur somewhere in the table. On a prior-year carry, line 3 is skipped and any old manual divisor is irrelevant.

Fact.Name: Monthly exclusion before final source validation
Fact.Description: Select the correctly carried prior-year line 4 only for an annuity that began before 2025; otherwise divide original investment by computed line 3. Never recalculate a carried monthly amount. This intermediate is not a filed result. The fresh-branch dividend is ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract, the cost after the IRC 72(e)(11)(A) box 8 long-term-care reduction, the same operand the legacy route divides; it equals the intake on every form without a code W box 8 charge. The completeness and non-negative checks still read the intake.

Fact.Name: Selected worksheet supported and internally consistent
Fact.Description: Complete supported-source confirmation and legal gates, nonnegative source amounts, 1-12 current months, original date/type, age or guarantee, prior-method choice and manual agreement are required. Post-1986 recovery cannot exceed cost; a 2025 start has no pre-2025 recovery. A pre-1987 start skips prior recovery. A fresh fixed-period contract must have at least thirteen monthly payments within a confirmed more-than-one-full-year arrangement, and cannot have fewer total payments than current months; age 75-or-older fixed contracts cannot guarantee 60 or more monthly payments. Positive contradictory rollover/disaster/Form 4972/NUA/death-benefit answers are excluded; unasked special facts are covered only by the scope confirmation, not an automatic audit.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 4 monthly tax-free amount
Fact.Description: Validated carried or freshly divided monthly exclusion. Dollar division retains the native cents HALF_EVEN behavior, matching the existing engine; the annual amount is rounded separately. Missing or inconsistent selected inputs stay Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 5 annual monthly exclusion
Fact.Description: Multiply line 4 by the number of months FOR WHICH the current payments were made; do not infer the count from checks received or remaining expected payments. Retain the existing whole-dollar annual reporting convention.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 7 remaining investment before this year
Fact.Description: For a start after 1986, original cost less all amounts recoverable tax-free in prior years (including omitted amounts that may need amended returns). Pre-1987 annuities skip line 7; no zero is fabricated for a skipped row. The minuend is ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract (IRC 72(e)(11)(A)), as on the legacy route.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 8 amount excluded this year
Fact.Description: Before 1987, use line 5 without a lifetime cost cap. For a start after 1986, use the lesser of the annual exclusion and the remaining investment. This is the worksheet line 8, not a new deduction from box 2a.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 9 taxable annuity for 2025
Fact.Description: The validated gross periodic pension minus line 8, floored at zero. This amount replaces rather than adds to the reported taxable box 2a, even if box 2a is smaller. It feeds the existing effectiveTaxableAmount and pension-income consumers; any existing properly applicable downstream exclusion remains separate. Line 1 is ../simplifiedMethodIncludibleGrossDistribution - box 1 rounded to whole dollars less the IRC 72(e)(11)(B) box 8 charge - the same line 1 the legacy route subtracts from; it equals rounded box 1 on every form without a code W box 8 charge. The validity gate still requires the box 1 intake itself to be answered and non-negative.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 10 cost recovered through 2025
Fact.Description: For an annuity starting after 1986, add prior recoverable cost and current line 8 for next-year records. Pre-1987 annuities skip this line, and it remains Incomplete/not applicable rather than a fictitious zero.

Fact.Name: Worksheet A line 11 unrecovered cost after 2025
Fact.Description: For a post-1986 start, original investment less line 10; zero signals full cost recovery. This is a carry-forward record, not an automatic deduction or historical-return correction. Pre-1987 annuities skip this row. The minuend is ../simplifiedMethodInvestmentInContract (IRC 72(e)(11)(A)), as on the legacy route.

Fact.Name: Legacy Simplified Method remaining cost
Fact.Description: Exact pre-existing unselected-method arithmetic, factored into a named operand for the existing schema. Not a new source-history calculation and not used to fill missing selected inputs.

Fact.Name: Legacy Simplified Method annual exclusion
Fact.Description: Exact pre-existing unselected-method arithmetic, factored into a named operand for the existing schema. Not a new source-history calculation and not used to fill missing selected inputs.

Fact.Name: Legacy Simplified Method total exclusion
Fact.Description: Exact pre-existing pre/post-1987 exclusion switch, given a name to replace a schema-invalid nested subtrahend. The unselected manual arithmetic and missing-input behavior are unchanged.
